subject: atlantic wolffish
title: This Fish Crushes Crabs and Urchins, Then Loses Its Teeth Every Year

scenes.text: This fish eats shells for a living, and every year its teeth fall out.
The Atlantic wolffish grows up to one and a half metres, in water near freezing.
It has long canine fangs at the front and rows of crushing teeth behind.
It uses them to smash crabs, whelks and spiny sea urchins, shells and all.
But once a year it loses those teeth and grows new ones. Until they harden, it can't eat.
Then the new set comes in, and it goes back to crunching.

description:
The Atlantic wolffish has large canines and rows of crushing teeth for eating crabs, whelks and sea urchins.
It loses its teeth and grows new ones each year, typically after the breeding season, and goes through a fasting period until the new set hardens. It also makes antifreeze proteins for water as cold as -1 degree C.
Would you want new teeth every year?
first_comment: The male guards a ball of up to 30,000 eggs, wrapping his body around it. What fish should we cover next?
